reconcile.note: Keil & Delitzsch read the repeated queen-mother formula as retained title for Maachah, making Asa her grandson rather than Abijam's brother.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Otto Thenius argued the repeated formula meant Abijam married his own mother, treating the verse as a corrupted text rather than evidence of a grandmother-regent.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Otto Thenius (1849), Die Bücher der Könige.

sides.snippet: Asa his son reigned in his place.
sides.verseText: Abijam slept with his fathers; and they buried him in the city of David: and Asa his son reigned in his place.

sides.snippet: his mother's name was Maacah the daughter of Abishalom.
sides.verseText: Forty-one years reigned he in Jerusalem: and his mother's name was Maacah the daughter of Abishalom.
